newsitem.title: USA: Nigerian rights activist arrives in U.S. - official.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian rights activist arrives in U.S. - official.

text.p: A human rights activist who has opposed Nigeria's military government arrived in the United States on Sunday after being detained at Lagos airport, a spokesman for his host organisation said.

Innocent Chukwuma, 30, a project director for the Civli Liberties Organisation, Nigeria's oldest and largest human rights association, was scheduled to arrive in the United States on Friday for the 1996 Reebok Human Rights Award ceremonies this week. He arrived late on Sunday, said Doug Cahn, a spokesman for the event.
"He's alright. He's in the United States. It turns out he was detained at Lagos Airpot (in Nigeria) for several hours, but eventually was released," Cahn said.

Chukwuma has been jailed twice in the past for challenging the polices of successive military regimes in Nigeria. He is scheduled to be one of four human rights activists to receive the 1996 Reebok Human Rights Award at a ceremony Wednesday, one day after Human Rights Day.
Africa's most populous nation is been under fire from Western countries over human rights and lack of democracy.
